inlines.v: MOB, noun [from Latin mobilis, movable, variable.] 1. A crowd or promiscuous multitude of people, rude, tumultuous and disorderly. 2. A disorderly assembly. Had every Athenian citizen been a Socrates, every Athenian assembly would still have been a mob 3. A huddled dress. MOB, verb transitive To attack in a disorderly crowd; to harass tumultuously. 1. To wrap up in a cowl or vail.
